messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.subject_clean: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

If you can get point estimates and error ellipses, then that's most of the challenge. The rest is formatting.

At the moment, the easiest way to get sigloc error ellipses into ctmm is probably:
Project the location point estimates from sigloc back to long-lat
Import the long-lat point estimates (with their timestamps) into ctmm as location data, but provide the same projection that was used in sigloc to calculate the error ellipses.
Copy over the sigloc variance/covariance columns into ctmm telemetry object columns COV.x.x,COV.y.y,COV.x.y
I think that should do it. You should be able to plot the location data and see their error ellipses the same as in sigloc.

I've read the paper sigloc is based on (Lenth, 1981) and a newer method (ATM: Gerber et al, 2018 <https://movementecologyjournal.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s40462-018-0129-1>). If there is demand, I could probably put something directly into ctmm. It looks like the sigloc package is no longer maintained and I was told that development completed on the ATM package as well.

Best,
Chris

On Wednesday, October 31, 2018 at 3:05:04 PM UTC-4, Chris Ward wrote:
> Hi Chris,
>
> I had originally discarded data with error ellipses I felt were too great for the work I was doing, but after having seen your talk at TWS a few weeks ago I am strongly considering trying to include all error into my analyses. Unfortunately, I can't figure out a way to do this in ctmm. I am using the r-package sigloc to triangulate locations, which gives variance in X, variance in Y, a covariance XY and an angle differential (?) as outputs for the estimate variance.
>
> If you have any advice on what direction I could go to tackle this, it would be greatly appreciated.
>
> Thank you!
>
> Chris

messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.subject_clean: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

Thanks for the feedback. sigloc operates using UTMs - so I am assuming the variance/covariance per location is in meters. In my import file, I had already converted my UTMs to lat/long before importing into ctmm for analysis. Are the variance/covariance columns in ctmm telemetry objects based off long-lat units, or meters, or can they be specified? It would save me a bit of work if I didn't have to run sigloc again (especially considering it is no longer maintained.)

I wasn't aware of ATM - thanks for that. I will look into it.

I think it would be useful to have a triangulation method for those researchers still using the VHF in ctmm. For many small animals, it is currently the only way to track - and $$$ will keep people using VHF for a while until costs come down for small GPS loggers. Although, with R, as long as packages are compatible with each other it may be redundant to write it in the package if it is already working in another package.

Thanks again,

Chris

messages.subject_clean: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I believe both sigloc and ctmm store the error ellipse information the same way, in square meters, just with different column names. I think you can copy them over directly if you use the same projection. I doubt the UTM projection, specifically, is necessary for sigloc to function, but some locally flat x-y projection is necessary.

Best,
Chris

messages.body_plain:
I am getting an error when working through the same code in Appendix S3 to create an IOU model. I am wondering if there may be a bug in the latest version? I am working off the github version downloaded 11/12/2018.

gabs <- buffalo[[2]]
gabsS <- gabs[901:1300, ]

#An example of manually specifying initial values via the ctmm function. #The values used for inits.iou were taken from the parameter sliders of #variogram.fit s.inits.iou <- ctmm(tau=c(Inf, 19000))

#Fit the IOU model
iou.s <- ctmm.fit(gabsS, CTMM=s.inits.iou)

Error in if (tau[1] > tau[2] && nu * dt > 0.8813736) { :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

The same error pops up when I did this with my own data as well. Any suggestion?

Thanks,
Briana

messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,
have you made progress with checking the error autocorrelation of the 1-second data generated by the e-obs tags? We have also collected some 1 second data using these tags on red kites and it would be interesting to hear your thoughs on the handling of such data!

Best wishes,
Jakob

Am Mittwoch, 30. Mai 2018 03:11:09 UTC+2 schrieb Christen Fleming:
> Hi Maryam,
>
> We do not yet model error autocorrelation. So far, for sampling down to 10-15 second intervals, I haven't personally seen any autocorrelation in modern GPS telemetry error, but I am about to look at some of new e-obs solar tags that collect 1 second data when the battery is full. I also know from the literature that older GPS data is supposed to have substantial error autocorrelation at under ~30 second intervals.
>
> For the future, when the kind of data that has autocorrelated error is being collected (maybe the new e-obs solar tags?), handling it will require calibration data to be collected. The HDOP values only account for the heteroskedasticity, not the autocorrelation. But, fortunately, the autocorrelation only emerges at very short timescales.
>
> Best,
> Chris
>
> On Tuesday, May 29, 2018 at 2:36:41 PM UTC-4, Maryam Teimouri wrote:
> >
> > Hi Chris,
> >
> >
> > I have a question regarding handling spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement errors in ctmm package.
> >
> > You take into account the autocorrelation of location data in the modeling, I am wondering if it includes autocorrelation of measurement errors as well.
> >
> > Are HDOP values enough for estimating the autocorrelation of measurement errors in the modeling?
> >
> >
> >
> > Thanks in advance,
> >
> > Maryam
> >

messages.subject: Re: Spatio-temporal autocorrelation of measurement error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jakob,

Unfortunately, I have not gotten my hands on entirely genuine calibration data of that nature. What I had access to was a tag on a bird that was supposed to be roosting, so I could not definitely say what was what... and the "errors" seemed suspiciously large to be as smooth/colored as they were. If you have any calibration data of that type, where you leave the tag out in a fixed spot over an extended period of time, I would like to take a look.

My suspicion, though, is that there is some threshold around 30 seconds at which you get normal GPS error autocorrelation and maybe a second threshold at which you get additional error autocorrelation from the device's Kalman filter. As this data becomes common, we will put tools in the package to account for the error autocorrelation, but first I need something to look at and play with.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: akde() grid arguement
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I would like to calculate AKDEs for each of my individuals on the same grid with the purpose of using overlap(). When I try to enter lists into the akde() function it fails because I have too many individuals and it requires a lot of memory. To overcome this I need to specify the grid in akde() and calculate the UDs for each individual separately.

Q. Is the grid parameter in akde() supported yet and if so can you help provide some guidance as how to define a grid for a list of telemetry objects that can be entered into akde()?

Best,
Jared

Hi Jared,

The problem is almost certainly that the default grid is too large and dense. The first things I would try are

Turning down the resolution argument. The default of res=10 is fairly high, but it needs to be >=1.
Make sure that all individuals are near each other. I've had users report similar problems and it turned out that they had one tracked individual that was in a completely different area---making all default grids necessarily huge.

If that doesn't work, I would double loop over individuals and calculate overlaps for every pair.

Best,
Chris

On Friday, November 23, 2018 at 10:28:24 AM UTC-5, jwilson...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I would like to calculate AKDEs for each of my individuals on the same grid with the purpose of using overlap(). When I try to enter lists into the akde() function it fails because I have too many individuals and it requires a lot of memory. To overcome this I need to specify the grid in akde() and calculate the UDs for each individual separately.
>
> Q. Is the grid parameter in akde() supported yet and if so can you help provide some guidance as how to define a grid for a list of telemetry objects that can be entered into akde()?
>
> Best,
> Jared

messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

A colleague and I are both running into the same issue with respect to our different datasets: when we convert a MoveStack object into a list of telemetry objects, we lose the individual identifier/animal id. Here is example code. We are each working with data imported from a csv file rather than MoveBank.

#Import GPS data with multiple individuals
data <- read.csv('gps_data_all.csv')
data$timestamp <- as.POSIXct(data$timestamp,format="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz="UTC")

#Covert to MoveStack
movedata <- move(x=data$longitude, y=data$latitude,
                 time=data$timestamp,
                 data=data,
                 proj=sp::CRS("+init=epsg:4326"),
                 animal=data$id)

#Test that animal id is retained in MoveStack object
movedata@trackId #shows vector of animal ids
movedata@idData #shows vector of animal ids alongside other attributes from original dataframe

#Convert to list of telemetry objects
telemdata <- as.telemetry(movedata, drop=FALSE, projection="+init=epsg:4326")

#Test that animal id is retained in Telemetry object
telemdata[[1]]@info # $identity "unknown" --> animal ID is lost
#when tested on buffalo data, buffalo[[1]]@info $identity "Cilla"

I tried making the id variable a factor and also character string. Do you see anything obvious that we're missing?

Thanks,
Briana
